findings.reason: Verified at next-auth-options.ts:121: the password check runs only when `!credentials.totpCode`, and the new branch at line 131 keys only on `backupCode`, so a valid backup code with any non-empty totpCode and an empty password logs in without the password.

Verified in two-factor-auth.tsx: `onOpenChange` only toggles `enableModalOpen` and never calls `onEnable`/invalidate, so Escape or an outside click after enabling leaves the switch and badge showing 2FA disabled while the server has it enabled, and the backup codes are no longer shown on the settings page.

The read-modify-write of backupCodes in the authorize path has no conditional update, so concurrent logins with the same code can both succeed; the race is real but narrow and needs the attacker to already hold the code.
The missing_backup_codes message does point users who have no codes to a settings page they cannot reach while logged out, which is a correct but marginal copy/UX concern.
BackupCode.tsx does export a function named TwoFactor, but this is a naming nit with no behavioural impact.
